options: The decrease in equity that results from a business's ordinary, core operations
An increase in equity from core operations
A type of asset that depreciates over time
Any cash payment the business makes, regardless of reason
questions.explain: An expense is the decrease in equity that results from the costs of running the business's core operations.

questions.q: What does the matching principle say about when an expense should be recorded?
options: Always in the period the cash is paid, no exceptions
Only at the end of the fiscal year
In the same period as the revenue it helped generate, regardless of when it was paid for
Expenses are never matched to any particular period
questions.explain: The matching principle requires expenses to be recorded in the same period as the revenue they helped produce.

questions.q: Fernhollow Grounds Co. uses $600 of electricity in March but doesn't pay the bill until April. In which month is the expense recorded?
options: April, when the cash is paid
It is split evenly between March and April
It is never recorded because the bill wasn't paid in the same month
March, when the cost was actually incurred
questions.explain: The expense belongs in March, matched to when the electricity was actually used, even though cash goes out in April.

questions.q: A company prepays $12,000 in January for a full year of insurance. How much is January's expense?
options: $12,000, the full amount, since cash was paid in January
$1,000 — one-twelfth of the total, with the rest recorded as a Prepaid Expense asset
$0, since nothing is ever expensed until the policy ends
$6,000, half of the total
questions.explain: Only the portion used up in that period becomes an expense; the remainder stays as a Prepaid Expense asset until used month by month.

questions.q: What is Oracle Fusion's period-close process largely designed to ensure, in relation to the matching principle?
options: That every expense belonging to a period is actually recorded in that period before the books are closed
That no expenses are ever recorded in any period
That cash payments and expenses are always recorded in the same month
That the matching principle is ignored in favor of simpler cash-based tracking
questions.explain: The period-close process exists to make sure all expenses (and revenues) that belong in a period are captured before that period's books are finalized.
